lines.text: You can take {G} off {WHEN}. {WHEN2} you'll want {GP} back, and maybe an extra layer. || Enjoy the warm bit. It's the part of today that flatters you most.
{G} can come off {WHEN}. {WHEN2} you'll want {GP} back, plus an extra layer. || More layers means less of you on show. Everyone wins.
Take {G} off {WHEN}, then put {GP} back on {WHEN2} with an extra layer on top. || Two outfits in one day. You struggle with one.
You can take {G} off {WHEN}. Bring an extra layer to wear with {GP} {WHEN2}. || Bulky, yes. Nobody was looking at you for the outfit anyway.
{G} can come off {WHEN}. {WHEN2} you'll want {GP} back, plus an extra layer. || By then you'll look like you got dressed in the dark. Warm, though.
{WHEN} {G} can come off. {WHEN2} you'll need {GP} again, and something warm on top. || Shivering isn't a personality, whatever you've been telling people.
{WHEN} {G} can come off. {WHEN2} you'll need {GP} again, and something warm on top. || Something warm, not something cute. I've seen you choose before.
You can take {G} off {WHEN}. Bring an extra layer to wear with {GP} {WHEN2}. || Spare clothes in a bag all day. You're basically a toddler with a forecast.
{G} can come off {WHEN}. {WHEN2} you'll want {GP} back, plus an extra layer. || It ends colder than it started. I checked while you checked the mirror.
Take {G} off {WHEN}, then put {GP} back on {WHEN2} with an extra layer on top. || Layering. Fashion people do it on purpose. You'll do it to stop shivering.
{WHEN} {G} can come off. {WHEN2} you'll need {GP} again, and something warm on top. || Do you own something warm that isn't a blanket? Asking for later.
{G} can come off {WHEN}. {WHEN2} you'll want {GP} back, plus an extra layer. || Three steps, in order. Your most organized day this month.
Take {G} off {WHEN}, put {GP} back on {WHEN2}. || All that effort to look the same at the end. You're used to that.
You can take {G} off {WHEN}. You'll want {GP} back {WHEN2}. || The one routine you'll actually stick to this week.
{G} can come off {WHEN}, but you'll want {GP} back {WHEN2}. || Folded over your arm, {GP} still outdresses you.
Take {G} off {WHEN}, put {GP} back on {WHEN2}. || Simple enough. I kept the instructions short for you.
{G} won't be needed {WHEN}, but you'll want {GP} on again {WHEN2}. || A few hours without {GP}. Try not to let the freedom go to your head.
{G} can come off {WHEN}. Keep {GP} handy for {WHEN2}. || Carrying {GP} for hours won't do much for your look. Neither did wearing it.
You can take {G} off {WHEN}. You'll want {GP} back {WHEN2}. || Think of the middle as an intermission. The show isn't great either way.
{G} won't be needed {WHEN}, but you'll want {GP} on again {WHEN2}. || I've planned your outfit for the whole day. Someone had to.
{WHEN} you can take {G} off, but you'll need {GP} again {WHEN2}. || So don't get attached to the lighter look. It wasn't working anyway.
Take {G} off {WHEN}, put {GP} back on {WHEN2}, and in between, try to look like someone who planned it.
{G} can come off {WHEN}, but you'll want {GP} back {WHEN2}. || You: 'It's warm now.' Me: 'Keep reading.'
{G} can come off {WHEN}. Keep {GP} handy for {WHEN2}. || Tip: {GP} goes back on the way it came off. I believe in you. Mostly.
{G} can come off {WHEN} and stays off. || That's {G} sorted. The rest of your look, I can't help with.
{G} can come off {WHEN}, and you won't need {GP} again today. || The weather's doing its part. Over to you. No pressure, I've seen your best.
Once {G} comes off {WHEN}, you can leave {GP} off. || The day improves. Whether you do is up to you.
You can take {G} off {WHEN}. You won't need {GP} again after that. || One less thing for you to look awkward in.
You can take {G} off {WHEN}. You won't need {GP} for the rest of the day. || A day that only gets better. Rare for you, so savor it.
Once {G} comes off {WHEN}, you can leave {GP} off. || Probably the last clothing decision you'll get right today.
You can take {G} off {WHEN}. You won't need {GP} for the rest of the day. || I've freed you from {G} for the day. Try to look like you deserve it.
{G} comes off {WHEN}. It cools a little later, but you won't need {GP} back. || Trust me over your instincts. Your instincts chose that outfit.
{G} can come off {WHEN} and stays off. || Leave {GP} behind. You're carrying enough already.
{G} can come off {WHEN} and stays off, so for once something in your life gets simpler as the day goes on.
You can take {G} off {WHEN}. You won't need {GP} again after that. || Layer: off. Weather: improving. You: under review.
Once {G} comes off {WHEN}, you can leave {GP} off. || I don't wear layers either, and I look great. Just saying.
Bring the winter coat. It gets colder {WHEN}. || Puffy and unflattering, yes. Still an upgrade on frozen.
Have the winter coat with you. You'll need it {WHEN}. || Hauling it around is the most you'll lift this week.
{WHEN} it gets cold enough for the winter coat. || Toughing it out won't make you look tougher. Just bluer.
Don't leave the winter coat behind. You'll want it {WHEN}. || I know it ruins the outfit. The outfit wasn't that good.
{WHEN} a jacket won't be enough, so bring the winter coat. || The jacket is cuter. You're not cute enough to freeze for it.
Have the winter coat with you. You'll need it {WHEN}. || You'll look like a sleeping bag with opinions. A warm one.
It gets colder {WHEN}, bring the winter coat. || Nobody's impressed by how little you can wear in the cold. Especially not me.
{WHEN} it gets cold enough for the winter coat. || Your sense of temperature is optimistic. Mine is correct.
Have the winter coat with you. You'll need it {WHEN}. || Yes, it doubles your width. You've never been shy about taking up space.
It gets colder {WHEN}, bring the winter coat. || You, now: 'I'll be fine.' You, {WHEN}: not fine.
Bring the winter coat. It gets colder {WHEN}. || I'd lend you one, but I don't have arms. Or a coat. Or any sympathy left.
Bring the winter coat: {WHEN} it's cold enough that how you look stops mattering. It never mattered much.
{WHEN} it gets cool enough for a sweater. || You'll post about 'sweater weather' like you invented fall.
Bring a sweater. It cools down {WHEN}. || Pick a nice one. Someone might have to look at you.
It cools down {WHEN}, so bring a sweater. || Any sweater will do. You've never let looks stop you before.
{WHEN} short sleeves won't be enough, so bring a sweater. || Your arms have been on display long enough. Everyone's ready.
It gets cooler {WHEN}, so take a sweater along. || Tie it around your shoulders and pretend you own a boat.
Bring a sweater. It cools down {WHEN}. || A sweater: the closest thing to a hug you'll get today.
Pack a sweater. You'll be glad to have it {WHEN}. || Soft, warm, and it covers most of you. A sweater does a lot for you.
It gets cooler {WHEN}, so take a sweater along. || Nobody hands out medals for short sleeves {WHEN}.
{WHEN} short sleeves won't be enough, so bring a sweater. || Even for you, whatever you tell people about running warm.
Pack a sweater. You'll be glad to have it {WHEN}. || Later-you says thanks. Now-you is probably rolling their eyes.
It gets cooler {WHEN}, so take a sweater along. || I've never worn a sweater. I've seen yours. I'm not missing much.
It cools down {WHEN}, so bring a sweater, preferably one that makes you look like you tried.
Bring a jacket. It cools down {WHEN}. || By then it'll be the most put-together part of you.
A sweater alone won't do {WHEN}, so bring a jacket. || Layers. They hide a lot. You'll appreciate that.
Bring a jacket along. You'll want it {WHEN}. || Yes, even if it clashes. Warm beats chic, and chic was never on the table.
It gets cooler {WHEN}, so bring a jacket along. || Carry it like you meant to. Confidence is free, and you could use some.
Bring a jacket. It cools down {WHEN}. || Draped over your arm, it'll make you look busier than you are.
A sweater alone won't do {WHEN}, so bring a jacket. || The sweater was trying its best. So were you, I assume.
{WHEN} it gets cool enough for a jacket. || Finally, a layer that does something for your shoulders.
It cools down {WHEN}, so bring a jacket. || Shivering isn't the look you think it is.
Bring a jacket. It cools down {WHEN}. || It's one jacket. You've carried heavier grudges.
Bring a jacket for {WHEN}. I'd carry it for you, but I have no arms and you have no excuse.
It cools down {WHEN}, so bring a jacket. || Jacket: five stars. Your judgment: pending.
Bring a jacket along. You'll want it {WHEN}. || Between us, I think the jacket is the best thing you own.
The heat eases {WHEN}, but it stays warm. || You'll look less like a melted candle. Slightly less.
It cools off a little {WHEN}, but stays warm. || Enough to stop glistening. Not enough to call it a glow-up.
{WHEN} the worst of the heat is over, but it stays warm. || You made it through. Not gracefully, I'd guess.
It's not as hot {WHEN}, but still warm. || Your face can go back to a normal color. Eventually.
The heat eases {WHEN}, but it stays warm. || Nothing to bring. Even you can manage that.
It cools off a little {WHEN}, but stays warm. || Not cool enough to make you good company yet.
It cools off a little {WHEN}, but stays warm. || Good news for everyone standing near you.
Some relief from the heat {WHEN}, but it stays warm. || You'll be almost pleasant again. Almost.
It's not as hot {WHEN}, but still warm. || Warm suits you better than hot. Low bar, but still.
The heat eases {WHEN}, but it stays warm. || I was never bothered. Some of us are built cool. Some of us are you.
The heat eases {WHEN}, but it stays warm, so you can stop pretending you love summer.
Some relief from the heat {WHEN}, but it stays warm. || Pro tip: a cold shower. For the heat, and for everyone else's sake.
Take the umbrella for now. The rain stops {WHENSTOP}. || You can hold an umbrella. That's one skill confirmed.
The rain stops later, but you'll want the umbrella for now. || An umbrella makes anyone look purposeful. Give it a go.
It keeps raining for a while, then stops. Take the umbrella. || Wet doesn't suit you. Dry barely does.
Take the umbrella for now. The rain stops later. || Later. Not the second you step outside. The weather doesn't revolve around you.
The rain eases off later, but bring the umbrella for now. || Sprinting between doorways isn't a plan. Not with your cardio.
The rain stops later, but you'll want the umbrella for now. || The rain has an end time. Your bad decisions don't seem to.
Later the rain stops. For now, keep the umbrella with you. || One of you has to look sharp, and it won't be you.
The rain eases off later, but bring the umbrella for now. || You've survived worse than rain. Your own haircuts, for example.
It keeps raining for a while, then stops. Take the umbrella. || Rain makes everyone look a bit miserable. Today you won't stand out.
Take the umbrella for now. The rain stops {WHENSTOP}. || Dry in here, by the way. Dry and good-looking. One of us manages both.
Keep the umbrella with you until the rain stops {WHENSTOP}, which is more commitment than you've shown anything this year.
Later the rain stops. For now, keep the umbrella with you. || Terms and conditions: the umbrella keeps you dry, not interesting.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP}. || The snow knows when to stop. A rare quality. You might study it.
It's snowing now, but it stops later. || Snow makes everything look better. Almost everything.
It stops snowing {WHENSTOP}. || Note the time. It's an appointment even you could keep.
It's snowing now, but it stops later. || You look great in snowflakes. Everyone does. It's cheating.
It stops snowing later. || The snow gives up. You beat it to that by years.
The snow stops later. || Then it turns gray and lumpy. Relatable, I'd guess.
It stops snowing {WHENSTOP}. || Precise, aren't I? You could try it sometime.
It's snowing now, but it stops later. || Pretty while it lasts. You know how that goes.
The snow eases off later. || Enjoy the view from the window. It's better than the one in the mirror.
The snow stops later. || Today's award for quitting while ahead goes to the snow. You were nominated.
It's snowing now, but it stops later. || Step one: look out the window. Step two: say 'wow'. Step three: that's your whole contribution.
It stops snowing {WHENSTOP}. || One of us in this room knew that. Hint: it's not you.
Expect snow {WHENP}. || Go ahead, panic-buy bread. It's the most decisive you'll be all week.
There's snow on the way {WHENP}. || A few inches, and you'll act like you survived a polar expedition.
Snow starts {WHENP}. || You're not ready. You're never ready. It's just snow.
Snow moves in {WHENP}. || Go on, tell everyone. You love being the one with news.
Snow starts {WHENP}. || In snow, everyone looks a bit ridiculous. Finally, a level playing field for you.
It starts snowing {WHENP}. || Wrap up. You're not as hardy as you like to think.
{WHENP} it will start to snow. || Perfect weather for staying in and calling it 'cozy' instead of 'lazy'.
There's snow on the way {WHENP}. || Every snowflake is unique. You'll still be the boring one out there.
Expect snow {WHENP}. || Your winter look is about to get worse. Puffier, at least.
It starts snowing {WHENP}. || I'll stay in here, perfectly dry and still handsome. Report back.
Snow moves in {WHENP}, which gives you a few hours to look like you own winter clothes.
Snow starts {WHENP}. || Rate your readiness from one to ten. Now subtract five. That's you.
There's no dry spell today. Bring the umbrella. || Today you have an excuse for looking like that. Use it.
The rain lasts all day, so keep the umbrella with you. || You'll be holding it all day. Finally, something to do with your hands.
It's raining all day. Bring the umbrella. || You won't melt. I checked your specs.
The rain doesn't stop today, so take the umbrella. || A day for staying in. You were born for this.
It rains all day, so bring the umbrella. || Open it before you step out. You're not quick enough for the other way.
It rains all day, so bring the umbrella. || Go anyway. Damp and late is just your usual, plus water.
There's no dry spell today. Bring the umbrella. || Today the weather's as reliable as you wish you were.
The rain lasts all day, so keep the umbrella with you. || Hold it up properly. Your posture could use the practice.
Take the umbrella. The rain keeps going all day. || Under an umbrella all day, nobody sees your face. Lucky them.
The rain doesn't stop today, so take the umbrella. || I'd lend you my dry spot in here, but you'd ruin the look.
It rains all day, so the umbrella goes with you everywhere, which is more company than you usually get.
It's raining all day. Bring the umbrella. || Forecast for you: damp, then damper, then grumpy.
It won't stop snowing today. || Snow muffles everything. Not you, unfortunately.
The snow doesn't stop today. || Next to all that white, you almost look tanned. Almost.
The snow keeps coming all day. || By tonight everyone looks like a wet dog. You've got a head start.
It's snowing all day. || Perfect light for a photo. Not of you, but the light's perfect.
The snow keeps coming all day. || It covers everything ugly out there. Stand outside long enough, you never know.
It's snowing all day. || One snowball and you'll need a lie-down. I've seen your arm.
The snow keeps coming all day. || Footprints fill in fast today. Nobody will know where you went. Not that anyone asked.
It's snowing all day. || Gray sky, white ground, pale you. A matching set.
The snow doesn't stop today. || Wrap up warm. Your charm won't do it.
It's snowing all day. || I'd build you a snowman, but it would come out better-looking than you. Awkward.
There's no break in the snow today. || Snow report: deep. You report: shallow, as usual.
It snows all day, which gives you the perfect excuse to do exactly as little as you'd planned anyway.
Rain for now, then a dry spell, then more rain {WHENP}. The umbrella stays with you. || The dry spell isn't an invitation. You read too much into things.
The rain pauses later but picks up again {WHENP}, so don't put the umbrella away. || Putting it away early would be very you. Optimistic and wrong.
The rain stops for a while later, then comes back {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella with you. || Damp, dry, damp. Your look won't improve at any stage.
It keeps raining for now, then takes a break. It's back {WHENP}, so keep the umbrella. || An umbrella all day. Finally, an accessory that makes you look organized.
Rain for now, then a dry spell, then more rain {WHENP}. The umbrella stays with you. || Sticking with something all day. New for you, but you'll manage.
The rain pauses later but picks up again {WHENP}, so don't put the umbrella away. || I said 'pauses'. You'll hear 'stops'. You hear what you want.
It rains for now, stops for a bit, and starts again {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella. || One trip, two rains. You've had worse luck. Mostly self-inflicted.
Later the rain takes a break, but it returns {WHENP}. Hang on to the umbrella. || The rain comes back. It's the only thing that keeps coming back for you.
Rain for now, then a dry spell, then more rain {WHENP}. The umbrella stays with you. || Fair warning. Which is more than you give anyone.
The rain pauses later but picks up again {WHENP}, so don't put the umbrella away. || I don't have an umbrella. I don't need one. I don't need you either, but here we are.
Rain for now, rain again {WHENP}, and in between a dry spell almost as short as your attention span.
It rains for now, stops for a bit, and starts again {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella. || Today's recipe: open, close, open. Even you can follow it.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP} and starts again {WHENP}. || Two rounds of snow. You can't handle one with dignity.
It snows for now, takes a break, and starts again {WHENP}. || The snow gets a second chance to make a first impression. You don't.
It keeps snowing for now, then takes a break. It's back {WHENP}. || Don't call the break 'spring'. You do this every February.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP} and starts again {WHENP}. || I've timed both. You've never timed anything right in your life.
It keeps snowing for now, then takes a break. It's back {WHENP}. || The break isn't long enough to make you presentable. Not you.
The snow stops for a while later, then comes back {WHENP}. || It knows when to leave and when to come back. Two skills you lack.
Snow for now, then a break, then more snow {WHENP}. || The break is your window. Use it, if you can be quick for once.
It keeps snowing for now, then takes a break. It's back {WHENP}. || More snow than sense out there. You'll fit right in.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP} and starts again {WHENP}. || Two snowfalls, one of you. Unfair fight, and the snow's winning.
The snow takes a break later and comes back {WHENP}. Your motivation only managed the first part.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP} and starts again {WHENP}. || You, at the break: 'It's over.' Me: 'Read the whole sentence.'
Snow for now, then a break, then more snow {WHENP}. || Today's plan: snow, pause, snow. Still better than yours.
Bring the umbrella. There's a shower {WHENP}. || Carrying an umbrella while it's dry. People will think you have your life together.
There's a short rain shower {WHENP}. Have the umbrella with you. || A short one. You've made bigger fusses about less.
A rain shower comes through {WHENP}, so take the umbrella. || It's a quick one. Quicker than you've ever been at anything.
Expect a rain shower {WHENP}. The umbrella's worth taking. || A short shower won't ruin your look. Your look got there first.
A rain shower comes through {WHENP}, so take the umbrella. || Getting caught in it isn't romantic. Not with your face.
Expect a rain shower {WHENP}. The umbrella's worth taking. || Small rain, small umbrella, small risk. Even you can do that math.
Bring the umbrella. There's a shower {WHENP}. || A bit of rain won't kill you. Looking damp for the rest of the day might, socially.
There's a shower passing through {WHENP}, so bring the umbrella. || I'd risk it. But I'm not the one who looks bad wet.
{WHENP} there's a rainshower, so the umbrella comes along. || A short shower is the weather being considerate. Take notes.
There's a short rain shower {WHENP}. Have the umbrella with you. || I've never needed an umbrella, or help looking good. You'll want both.
Bring the umbrella. There's a shower {WHENP}. || A) Bring it. B) Get wet. C) Whatever you usually pick.
Bring the umbrella, there's a shower {WHENP}, and no, you can't outrun it. I've seen you hurry.
Pack the umbrella. Rain sets in {WHENP} and doesn't let up. || Anything you meant to do outside, do it before then. Or keep putting it off. That's your strength.
The rain starts {WHENP} and doesn't stop. Bring the umbrella. || You'll call it drizzle. Denial suits you.
Rain arrives {WHENP} and stays, so take the umbrella. || Hold it high. It's the most anyone's looked up to you.
It starts raining {WHENP} and keeps going, so bring the umbrella. || Good news: rain flatters nobody. You lose nothing.
{WHENP} the rain sets in for good. Bring the umbrella. || Enjoy the dry bit. It's as good as you'll look today. Low bar.
It starts raining {WHENP} and keeps going, so bring the umbrella. || A day like this needs a good attitude. Bring the umbrella instead.
The rain starts {WHENP} and doesn't stop. Bring the umbrella. || The big umbrella, not the tiny one. You need all the cover you can get.
{WHENP} the rain sets in for good. Bring the umbrella. || Gray skies for the rest of the day. Finally, lighting that's kind to you.
Rain arrives {WHENP} and stays, so take the umbrella. || It shows up and doesn't leave. You know the type. You are the type.
The rain starts {WHENP} and doesn't stop. Bring the umbrella. || I'll be in here, dry and smug. You'll be out there, damp and you.
It rains from {WHENP} on, so bring the umbrella and lower your expectations, which shouldn't take long.
Pack the umbrella. Rain sets in {WHENP} and doesn't let up. || Packing list: umbrella, patience, good attitude. You have one of those.
It might rain {WHENP}, so an umbrella wouldn't hurt. || Your luck isn't great, though. I've seen your outfits.
Rain {WHENP} is possible but not likely. The umbrella is up to you. || Up to you. That's what worries me.
There's a chance of rain {WHENP}. An umbrella wouldn't hurt. || Neither would a mirror check, but here we are.
Rain is possible {WHENP}, so maybe take the umbrella. || I'd decide for you, but then you'd have nothing to overthink.
It could rain {WHENP}. Take the umbrella to be safe. || A wet you is a sad you. A sad you is a lot. Just take it.
Rain is possible {WHENP}, so maybe take the umbrella. || I'm not saying it'll rain. I'm saying you'd look terrible if it did.
Rain {WHENP} is possible but not likely. The umbrella is up to you. || Trust your gut. Actually, no. Check your track record first.
It might rain {WHENP}, so an umbrella wouldn't hurt. || If it stays dry, you carried it for nothing. Welcome to most of your efforts.
It could rain {WHENP}. Take the umbrella to be safe. || Take it. Getting rained on won't make you more interesting.
Rain {WHENP} is possible but not likely. The umbrella is up to you. || Flip a coin. Heads, take it. Tails, take it. You're not great at chance.
It might rain {WHENP}, so an umbrella wouldn't hurt. || If I had hands, I'd pass it to you. Then I'd wash them.
It probably won't rain {WHENP}, but you've built a whole life on 'probably', so take the umbrella.
It's a bit cool for shorts now, but {WHEN} you'll be glad to have them. || Whether anyone else is glad to see your knees is another matter.
It starts cool, but it's shorts weather {WHEN}. || Pale legs on a cool morning. You'll glow. Not in a good way.
It's cool now, but {WHEN} it's warm enough for shorts. || Long pants would hide more. Hiding things has served you well.
Shorts could be worth it today. It's cool now, but warm {WHEN}. || A cold first hour builds character. You could use some.
It's a bit cool for shorts now, but {WHEN} you'll be glad to have them. || Your legs will hate me. Your legs don't get a vote.
{WHEN} it's warm enough for shorts, so think about putting them on now. || Yes, people will stare for a bit. They'd stare anyway.
A cool start, then shorts weather {WHEN}. || Shorts before it's warm. Brave, and a little sad. Very you.
Shorts could be worth it today. It's cool now, but warm {WHEN}. || I'm only suggesting. Your legs, your shame.
It's a bit cool for shorts now, but {WHEN} you'll be glad to have them. || Shiver now or sweat later. You've done both badly before.
It starts cool, but it's shorts weather {WHEN}. || I have no legs, so this is unbiased advice. Mostly. I've seen yours.
A cool start, then shorts weather {WHEN}. || Your legs: 'No.' Me: 'Yes.' You: still deciding.
Shorts could be worth it today. It's cool now, but warm {WHEN}. || Pros: comfort later. Cons: your legs, in public, now.
It warms up {WHEN}, so the winter coat can come off. || Nobody will notice. They weren't looking at you in the coat either.
The winter coat can come off {WHEN}. || You'll look smaller. Finally, something about you that's understated.
You can take the winter coat off {WHEN}. || The coat comes off and suddenly you're an optimist. Don't get carried away.
You'll be fine without the winter coat {WHEN}. || Your arms will remember they can move. Your brain, we'll see.
The winter coat can come off {WHEN}. || Then you'll stand around holding it like a dead animal. Classy.
It warms up {WHEN}, so the winter coat can come off. || Coat off. Now you just need a personality to replace it.
{WHEN} it's warm enough to lose the winter coat. || Try to look like someone who planned for this. You've had all winter.
It warms up {WHEN}, so the winter coat can come off. || Your inner thermostat was never good. Trust mine.
You'll be fine without the winter coat {WHEN}. || Out of the coat, into the light. Brave of you, all things considered.
You can take the winter coat off {WHEN}. || I've never worn a coat. Look how well I turned out. Learn from me.
The winter coat comes off {WHEN}, and with it your best excuse for walking like a penguin.
It warms up {WHEN}, so the winter coat can come off. || Breaking: local person sees own arms for the first time in months.
The scarf can come off {WHEN}. || Your neck is back. Nobody missed it, but it's back.
{WHEN} you won't need the scarf any more. || Three times around your neck was never a look. Now it's not even needed.
You'll be fine without the scarf {WHEN}. || The scarf was hiding a lot. Not enough, but a lot.
{WHEN} it's mild enough to lose the scarf. || One less thing making you look interesting.
{WHEN} you won't need the scarf any more. || One layer down. You're still mostly coat, which is for the best.
It warms up {WHEN}, so the scarf can come off. || Don't wave it around like you've won something. It got a bit warmer. That's it.
{WHEN} it's mild enough to lose the scarf. || Small progress, but more than you usually make.
You can take off the scarf {WHEN}. || Your face now goes all the way down to your collar. Bold.
You'll be fine without the scarf {WHEN}. || Your chin's been hiding in there for hours. It's allowed out. On probation.
The scarf can come off {WHEN}. || I've never needed a scarf. My frame keeps me looking sharp. Yours doesn't.
It warms up {WHEN}, so the scarf can come off and your neck can face the public again, as unprepared as ever.
{WHEN} it's mild enough to lose the scarf. || Your neck: 'Finally.' Everyone else: 'Oh. Your neck.'
